identity: University of Amsterdam full-time bachelor Modern Greek Language and Culture, RIO 56814, registry row 435. Current guide page 39685 gives Dutch, English and Modern Greek components. Athens is selected from the dated course entry’s two specified exchange destinations under the neutral order rule.
components: The first year also requires a Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring continues throughout the programme. These requirements carry no credits.
Rome’s successor: 1000 years of Byzantine Empire
The Human World: Introduction to the Humanities
A World of Regions: Introduction to Area Studies
Greece and Cyprus: From the Ottoman Period to the Present
Students need Modern Greek at A2 level. The first-year language courses prepare for reading and discussing Greek literary texts.
Philosophy of Science: National Identity, Borders and Territory
Memory and Conflict: Greece, Turkey and Cyprus
Venice, Byzantium and the Greek World
Study Abroad in Modern Greek Language and Culture

This example uses the Athens exchange route. The 30 EC combines 12 EC of language study at B1 or above with 18 EC in regional subjects. The course recommends at least 54 EC of year one and attendance in the first semester of year two. An approved home programme is available.
The Mediterranean and Europe: Contacts, Conflicts, Confluences
Students must command Modern Greek and Dutch at B1 level. The course uses Greek journalistic texts to study Greece, Cyprus and Europe.
Travel, Nostalgia and Cultures of Resistance in the Mediterranean
Use this 30 EC for a minor or an approved combination of electives, a placement or study abroad.
Bachelor’s Thesis in Modern Greek Language and Culture
Complete the first and second years before starting the thesis. The individual study is written in Dutch or English and includes an oral presentation.

sourceResolution: The complete dated curriculum matches the listed 180 EC. The public overview mentions Greece or Cyprus. The detailed exchange course specifies Athens and Thessaloniki and the guide introduction lists those two institutions, so this route uses first-listed Athens. Its allocation is 12 EC of B1-or-higher Greek and 18 EC in regional language, literature or cultural subjects. The home alternative is acknowledged separately and is not stacked. The third-year elective group is 30 EC. Faculty OER A6.4 and A6.6 set the ordinary full-time BSA threshold at 48 EC from year one.

progression.yearOne: Four 6 EC language courses progress from A1 to A2/B1, preparing for the A2 language-and-literature course in year two. The other 36 EC includes Byzantine history, Ottoman-to-modern Greek history, humanities and regional methods and Project Athens. Mandatory writing diagnostic and recurring tutoring carry zero credits.
progression.yearTwo: Two 6 EC language-and-literature courses, philosophy of science, memory/conflict and Venice-Byzantium regional history total 30 EC. The subsequent 30 EC exchange recommends at least 54 first-year EC and attendance in the first semester of year two. Full first-year completion and all five first-semester courses meet the stated preparation. Course 57916 specifies 12 EC language at B1 or higher and 18 EC regional subjects, with tutor consultation for deviations from regional subject selection. Its January first-year Erasmus application precedes departure by one year.
progression.yearThree: Three 6 EC thematic courses plus 30 EC of profiling and a 12 EC individual thesis give 60 EC. The Greece, Cyprus and Europe entry requires Greek and Dutch at B1. The language-and-literature sequence and the subsequent B1-or-higher exchange provide the Greek preparation, and the Dutch-taught route requires Dutch competence. The thesis requires both year one and year two to be completed. It is written in Dutch or English and includes an oral presentation. Optional placement is part of profiling space rather than a separate mandatory component.
